Look at the number of charges left on the Serum to see how many times you can do this. You can recharge it by putting it back in a Polymerizer. So if you ever get a magic recipe, you can just leave a Serum Array of it around and just recharge it as you need it.

[note]You cannot recharge Serums using a Thaumic Restorer.[/note]

nodes.name: To Play God
nodes.desc:
In order to continue with bees, to mutate and breed them as you like, you need mutagen. This greenish, smelly liquid needs to be refined from bacterial sludge that seems to be most readily available from fluid pockets on Mars. You will be able to continue, once you've acquired this.

In the meantime you can start working with the Genetics mod, since we all know Gendustry is too easy... Check out the recipes and you'll understand why you should look into the Genetics mod.

[note]Make sure to make more with the Vat once you can actually make it.[/note]

nodes.name: Highend species: Draconic
nodes.desc: On your way to awesome bees, you have to collect only the best traits available.

nodes.name: Figuring Out Butterflies
nodes.desc: Butterflies don't do much, but this analyzer will give you details on their abilities.

nodes.name: Alvearies
nodes.desc:
The alveary is an advanced variant of the apiary. The alveary allows for combs to be produced faster due to its natural speed increase to production (as well as the ability to add up to six frames via the Extra Bees frame housings) and due to its ability to be modified by other blocks.

It is possible to adjust the internal temperature of the alveary using the alveary heater or alveary fan in order to accommodate bees that require hotter or colder climates.

Certain bees will not produce their specialty items unless they are Jubilant. This requires matching their preferred Temperature/Humidity, without any genetic modifiers. Some bees also need a block of something beneath them as well.

It is also possible to use mutators to increase chances of mutation, alveary lighting and alveary rain shield to allow bees without the nocturnal and tolerant flyer traits to work during the night and rain, respectively, and the swarmer to use excess royal jelly to create princesses that last for a limited number of generations.

[note]If you're mutating bees that need a specific block in it, you need to place the required block under the middle bottom, and have the one directly above be a normal alveary block.[/note]

nodes.name: Polymeriser
nodes.desc:
The Polymeriser is necessary to turn Serum into something you can actually inject into a Larvae. It has a bonus use of strengthening an isolated gene so it can be sequenced faster by a factor of 4x.

The Polymeriser requires Raw DNA and Polymerising Bacteria. Raw DNA is obtained from the Genepool, and Polymerising Bacteria is made from incubating bacteria with bone meal. Gold nuggets can be used as a catalyst to speed up the process. You can also make more Polymerising Bacteria by feeding it back into an Incubator with Growth Medium.

When using the Polymeriser to prepare some Serum for a Larvae, the result will have a number of "charges." In other words, you get multiple uses out of it. This is nice because you are going to need to make a bunch of drones if you are trying to get all those traits to stick. Remember that you cannot use this process to modify a princess or queen directly! If you are satisfied before you use up all the Serum, you can recycle it by passing it through a smelter/furnace of your choice.

It takes two minutes to polymerise stuff. If you already use a World Accelerator for sequencing, then the Polymeriser would also benefit from cuddling up with that accelerator on another side.

nodes.name: Blank Gene Samples
nodes.desc:
To get the various traits from a bee, you need a lot of power, labware and an empty gene sample. You don't need a lot of those, as you can just throw them in a furnace to remove remaining DNA of traits you don't need or want.

In the meantime you can start working with the Genetics mod, since we all know Gendustry is too easy... Genetics is used for bees, trees, and Botany flowers so it gets its own quest tab. Gendustry is really good for bees, but will require top tier equipment.

nodes.name: Breeding Bees Into Oblivion
nodes.desc:
If bee breeding is a dice game, then these are the biggest factors you'd control to win:

1. Fertility: How many dice you can roll each turn.
2. Mutation Rate: How good of a roll you need to make.
3. Lifespan: How often you can play the game.

The Oblivion Frame dramatically helps with #3 by reducing the bee's lifespan to the point that you can play the breeding dice game in one "tick" of 27.5 seconds. A bee with the "Shortest" lifespan trait cycles for 10 ticks (275 seconds), so you'd minimally cut the cycle by a whole order of magnitude!

You can find Oblivion Frames in Stronghold libraries. This is how you can get them in the early game for very aggressive bee breeding. Later, you can make them from Dragon Eggs. These frames are very precious and you don't want their durability to run out. A typical repair method is to use a Thaumic Restorer on them.

Wait, to find a Stronghold reliably, I need some Eyes of Ender, and that's an HV-tier Chemical Reactor recipe! If you happen to have a Large Chemical Reactor, remember that it overclocks perfectly, so you can crank er' up with a bunch of MV-tier Energy Input Hatches.

The Oblivion Bee Meta

The oblivion bee meta can be enough to breed most bees quickly. You could do the whole bee breeding quest line with it, but you can ultimately improve on it with Alvearies and genetic modification. What you need for this meta is:

1. An Apiary
2. An Oblivion Frame
3. Some way to repair the frame (typically: thaumic restorer)
4. A Beealyzer and a lot of honey

This is a hands-on process. You don't automatically send the princess and drones back through because you need to watch the oblivion frame's durability. You inspect all the offspring bees after each cycle and hand-pick which to try next after a pass through the Beealyzer.

You can accelerate the Apiary with a World Accelerator. [warn]Be sure to protect the World Accelerator and supporting equipment from rain![/warn] You can use glass or a breakable clear glass so the Apiary can still see the sky while the World Accelerator is protected. If you need to use batteries, you can use a State Cell to draw out a button pulse to the world accelerator so it runs juuust long enough for an accelerated cycle.

nodes.name: Only the Best: Speed Blinding
nodes.desc: On your way to awesome bees, you have to collect only the best traits available. Buzz buzz buzz, working hard and really buzzing!

nodes.name: Upgraded Home
nodes.desc:
The Bee House can be used to stabilize mutations, for example if you have successfully bred two different bees, but the passive traits are different from the active ones.

To actually breed those together to get a new species, you'll need something different - the Apiary. Building them will require a Carpenter and Impregnated frames, along with Seed Oil and Creosote - quite a bit of industrialization! Or, if you're lucky, you can find a beekeeper villager to trade with. Maybe you can help the villagers get lucky to make more beekeeper villagers? If only Cupid and his bow were around...

Production rates in an empty Apiary are low - lower than a Bee House by quite a bit, in fact. But the Apiary has two big advantages - Frames, and Automation. You can now use your Untreated or Impregnated frames in here to boost output - and the boost is multiplied. So 3 x2 frames gives you 2 * 2 * 2 = 8x extra output! You can also automate I/O for the bees and their products, though not frames unfortunately.

Bees also don't live as long as in a Bee House, but that's actually a good thing.

Also, you should check the Genetics mod for useful machines. The Acclimatiser can give very picky bees a much wider temperature or humidity tolerance without having to breed it into them.

nodes.name: Pollen Collection Kit
nodes.desc: The easy way to get some pollen, just right-click on leaves. The Pollen Collection Kits are one-time use though, so maybe make a few.

nodes.name: Lab Stand
nodes.desc:
The Lab Stand is a block on which an Apiarist Database, Arborist Database, Botanist Database or Gene Database can be placed by right-clicking on the placed stand with the database, attaching it and allowing the database to be accessed by right-clicking on the stand.

This is not a required structure, but people like to put their Gene Database on one as a kind of trophy case.

nodes.name: A New Home
nodes.desc:
Now that you've destroyed the poor bees' homes, you should build them a new one. The humble Bee House will not let your bees mutate into new species. But you'll need the combs anyways for better housing. The production rate isn't too bad, but they cannot be automated.

One tip - Put some vanilla saplings near the Bee Houses. Bee Houses give a natural boost of 3x to pollination vs better housing. The bees will pollinate them and you might get lucky and start getting some Forestry tree crossbreeding. Stick with Oak and Birch trees, they'll give you a nice mix of starter Forestry trees.

Of course, if you do this without taking precautions, you may find yourself swarmed by laggy butterflies...

You may also notice that bees with the 'flower' type flower spread flowers. This can be used to get, say, lavender, among others. If you don't like them spreading them everywhere, replace the dirt/grass blocks, remove the trait, or reduce the pollination speed/territory.

nodes.name: Only the Best: Cave
nodes.desc: On your way to awesome bees, you have to collect only the best traits available. Bees with Cave can work in housing that is covered - by more housing!

nodes.name: Growth Medium
nodes.desc:
The Binnie's Genetics machines will rely on Growth Medium in either a little, or a lot. If you can't make too much of it, then you'll need to rely on other passive generation to keep the machines constantly supplied for researching genes. If you can make a lot of Growth Medium, then you can use it in a closed loop in Incubators to duplicate some of the mod's resources you have previously produced just once.

It requires:
* Sugar: The easy one here, and remember multiple bee species can produce it too.
* Bones (whole bones, not meal): mob farm, animal traps, goofy conversions.
* Wood Ash: Smelt some saplings.
* Mulch: There are a lot of ways to do this, but consider Peat bees since you're already going for the bees.

This quest is just a little nudge that you should passively produce Growth Medium, which means being able to passively produce all of these ingredients.

nodes.name: A Chest for...Butterflies? Really?
nodes.desc: Store your completely useless butterflies in this.

nodes.name: Welcome to Biology Class!
nodes.desc:
Binnie's Genetics mod will allow you to pick and chose traits for bees, trees and Botany flowers. But not for free! Doing this comes at a price.

[note]Note: We'll be focusing just on the bees in this section.[/note]

You will need a few streams of resources you can automate into passive generation. These are used across the process in different machines for different purposes, but Growth Medium is a super-resource you can substitute for some of the steps if you're able to produce that in abundance.

The research process can be easily automated. Gene modification and drone generation can be automated, but are slow and infrequent enough that you will probably just attend to them when you need them.

The general idea is to sequence a pile of leftover drones until you get all the traits you want from it. You'll then have those traits forever and can inject your own combinations of everything you've found into drone Larvae to make new drones that carry those traits. Larvae hatch only into drones. You don't get to directly hatch princesses and queens, so you have to worry about these new traits sticking across generations.

These genetic edits don't let you create new traits out of thin air. They just let you pick and choose what you have already researched, and that has to come out of bees you already have. You may use this to set up all your production bees through the rest of the game, but traits like 4x fertility also help with breeding.

You'll want to prepare a lab workspace for this. The actual machines won't take too much space. In fact, you'll probably wind up smacking a bunch of them against world accelerators, which will require direct contact due to using Tile Entity mode. What will end up taking up more space is any passive resource generation you prepare to make the process more hands-free.

You will need an alveary with a hatchery to produce Larvae of the base bee you want to modify.

These machines require RF power. It's recommended to provide power to an Ender IO capacitor and power these machines with RF instead of powering directly with GT EU. You can connect GT EU power up to these, but you run into strange consumption from amperage conversion glitches, or machines not getting power despite looking like they have proper cabling.

Ultimately, you'll need at least 7 of these casings and could end up making 14+ casings for all the machines you may opt to produce. You will also need HV-tier circuit production. There is one EV circuit involved in the complete process too.

[note]We give special credit to Three for a video explaining all these machines and their interplay:

An Early Game Guide to Genetically Modify your Bees in Gregtech: New Horizons
[url]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EmhDlga2SCA[/url]

Note that he will rant about the quest book. That was--ahem--an older version of the quest book.[/note]

nodes.name: Registry
nodes.desc: The Registry combines the existing four databases into a new sleek browser to allow the properties, mutations and genes of all discovered bees, trees, butterflies and flowers.

nodes.name: Master Registry
nodes.desc: The master beekeeper needs a master registry. Make sure you don't get any tears in your apiaries as you collect all the requirements!

nodes.name: Fluorescent Dye
nodes.desc:
Here is another one requiring ingredients you'll want to passively generate. The Sequencer needs one (1) Fluorescent Dye per gene it sequences. Each one is made from one of each tossed into a Mixer:

* redstone
* glowstone
* orange dye
* yellow dye
* molten blaze (from blaze powder)

Given how many bees you'll end up sequencing to get all the key genes you want, expect to need at least some hundreds or even thousands of these. Yes, there are only so many actual genes, but you're going to be hitting duplicates.

nodes.name: Only the Best: Tree Breeding
nodes.desc: For those who love Forestry trees.

nodes.name: X-Men, or Should I Say X-Bee?
nodes.desc:
The Mutator can vastly accelerate genetic mutations, even allowing those ultra rare bees to be bred. Items inserted into the Mutator control how much mutation it causes.

Soul Sand - 50 percent increase
Ender Pearl - 100 percent increase
Eye of Ender - 300 percent increase

nodes.name: Genetic Imprinter
nodes.desc:
With this powerful machine, you can inject gene samples, which allows you to alter any aspect of your bee, tree or butterfly. The gene sample (or pattern) will not be destroyed.

The machine has a 40% chance to kill ignoble bees.

One labware is consumed per operation.

nodes.name: Go Find Some Bees
nodes.desc: The next thing to do: Find a few bee hives around the world. There are 11 mundane bees that can be found, of which 8 are located in the Overworld. Any kind of bee will work for this quest.

nodes.name: Bees By the Millions
nodes.desc:
If you need endgame high speed production, industrial apiaries are the way to go. Industrial Apiaries take upgrade frames that never break. Production frames can be stacked up to 8 high. It also has many options for emulation, more pollen retrieval, and others.

The Industrial Apiary is now a GT machine. It takes up to UV voltage and up to 4 amps but the base usage is just 37 EU/t. You can no longer use a World Accelerator and there is only the one machine, so no GT overclocking. Instead, there are new acceleration upgrades that act similar to a World Accelerator but are directly integrated into the machine. You will want to use them, they increase the speed and energy usage by a lot. The final tier also increases productivity.

But I shouldn't drone on too long. Go make one and find out yourself.

nodes.name: Mutatron
nodes.desc:
Mutations can be boring, they can be annoying, and most times, they are frustrating. With this machine, you will get a 100 percent pure bred mutation. If the combination of princess and drone can result in multiple mutations, the outcome is random. But who cares?

[note]You can now upgrade your leftover Bees Advanced bags to Bees Expert in the last quest tab.

If you missed grabbing an effect from a species, this is a way to get it again.

You'll need naquadah bees to make this, and the other Gendustry machines.[/note]

nodes.name: Silky Combs and Propoli
nodes.desc:
Collect silky combs and extract some silk wisp out of it in order to make some Apiarist's clothes.

This can take a very long time, so parallelize!

Use a GregTech or Forestry Centrifuge to get Silky Propoli. For higher tier (and useful) combs you need a GT centrifuge.

nodes.name: Incubator
nodes.desc:
The Incubator is a general production machine that serves two purposes:

1. Hatching (modified) Larvae into drones at the end of the whole process.
2. Heating items and liquids to produce different resources you will need in different parts of the entire research and modification process.

There are up to five different resources you can create from Incubators:

1. Liquid Growth Medium: Water + Growth Medium
2. Bacteria: Liquid Growth Medium + Wheat OR more Bacteria + Growth Medium
3. Enzyme: Bacteria + Sugar
4. Bacteria Vector: Bacteria + Blaze Powder OR more Bacteria Vector + Growth Medium
5. Polymerizing Bacteria: Bacteria + Bone Meal OR more Polymerizing Bacteria + Growth Medium

Three of the recipes can optionally be extended by injecting them with more Growth Medium instead of using a different ingredient. If you're able to produce a bunch of Growth Medium, consider "priming" incubators for these outputs and then switching them to use Growth Medium indefinitely in a feedback loop.

Enzyme is usually produced in a pipeline from Bacteria, which is in turn produced from Liquid Growth Medium.

Bacteria Vector is only used by the Inoculator to modify Larvae, and you don't need it if you use a Splicer instead.

PS: You'll also need a source for Ethanol for the Genepool and the Isolator. This technology line has a drinking problem.

PPS: Blaze Powder also comes up with at least Fluorescent Dye later.

nodes.name: Diamondware
nodes.desc: Also known as labware. Be prepared. In order to do serious bee-work, you need stacks of diamonds. I'm not joking, stacks! Better start working on that diamond bee!

nodes.name: Genetic Transposer
nodes.desc:
DNA samples of species and/or traits are pretty valuable. You always should keep at least one of each gene sample you get your hands on in a chest somewhere safe. By using this machine, you are able to copy any gene sample, for the cost of an empty serum vial and some labware.

[note]You don't actually need to keep all of them if you don't intend to use them of course.[/note]

nodes.name: First Things First
nodes.desc: As usual. In order to get started with bees, you need a few basic things. Most importantly... a scoop. For this quest you want to make a GregTech scoop. Later you can make scoops using magic or even rechargeable scoops.

nodes.name: Making Bees More Comfortable
nodes.desc:
The Acclimatiser can widen the temperature tolerance of a bee. This is technically a little side quest with Binnie's Genetics machines, but these alterations are permanent and carry into their genome.

Note that the bee's species determines its favored temperature for jubilance. You can't use this to make a bee produce secondary products in a different climate.

Drones, princesses, queens, and even larvae can go in these machines. This means you can boost one queen and be set for life for that bee.

(You can also use it for pollen, butterflies, caterpillars, plants...)

When a specimen's tolerance has been pushed as far as it can go, that bee will go in the output slot. The typical thing to do here is pipe the bee automatically into another Acclimatiser like a little trauma conga line. At the end, the bee should be able to tolerate being anywhere.

Here's what you can use for what at what factors:
* Temperature down
  * ice: 0.75
  * snowball: 0.15
* Temperature up
  * lava (canned!): 0.75
  * blaze powder: 0.5
  * blaze rod: 0.75
* Humidity up:
  * water (canned!): 0.75
* Humidity down:
  * sand: 0.15

Fluid containers are consumed. If only you had a waxy substance in overabundance you could use for throwaway fluids!

[note]The Ole' "Both Trick": If your specimen already has at least Up/Down 1 for temperature or humidity, acclimatizing it in the opposite direction will make it Both 1. The trick is that it'll now grow both ways for the price of expanding only in one.

So, if handling canned water and lava is annoying, and you can start with Up 1 for temperature and humidity, then you can just bombard it with temperature and humidity lowering steps. It'll switch to Both 1 and then eventually Both 5 without ever raising temperature or humidity again.

This lets you skip out on canning liquids, you sly dog.
[/note]

nodes.name: Death to Bees!
nodes.desc: These frames will let you kill your bees faster. It's to breed the next generation sooner, right? Not because you don't like them?

nodes.name: Analyze Them All
nodes.desc:
Every bee has multiple properties that define what the bee does, how it behaves in rain or at night, and a couple of other aspects. It is mandatory to keep track of those properties. This kit isn't very good since it doesn't give you information on their Inactive attributes, but waste not, want not.

You'll need to use paper to analyze each bee.

nodes.name: Are the Bees Buzzing, or Screaming?
nodes.desc:
These frames cause mutations at an increased rate. They're super useful.

About the stats on frames you see when holding shift, you'll note that some have a different number in brackets next to them, this means that this is the maximum they can be stacked. This only applies to the Extra Bees ones.

The stats on the frames are also multiplicative instead of additive, so after 4 frames in an alveary, soul frames will max out. On the other hand, accelerated frames will take 9 to get there, but you can just keep on going.

If you pile up the multipliers, 5x from stimulator, 3x from mutator, and 4x1.8x frames, it'll get you to 157x, getting you those 1% bees in a single generation!

nodes.name: Upgrading the Alveary
nodes.desc:
These basic upgrades to the Alveary make it more powerful.

Frame Housing - Automation-enabled frame slot for the Alveary. Uses 5 durability every bee tick (27s). If it runs out on that tick, it has no effect.
Alveary Stabilizer - Prevents the bees from mutating into another species. Ideal for breeding traits into a line.
Alveary Transmission - Power input for upgrades that use power.
Alveary Sieve - Instead of the pollen from a bee fertilizing a nearby tree, it is stored here and can be manually applied. Requires manually placing woven silk in the inventory.
Swarmer - Creates additional Ignoble queens in hives around the Alveary. These are genetic copies of the original. This uses Royal Jelly or Aromatic Lumps. The latter are more effective.

[note]Note that all upgrade blocks must be in the bottom 2 layers. The center block also cannot be an upgrade block, though the bottom center can.[/note]

[warn]When using power, the transmission block will suck down entire amps to fill a tiny amount. Use the EnderIO capacitors or something similar to prevent this.[/warn]

nodes.name: Bee More Knowledgeable
nodes.desc: This database keeps track of everything bee.

nodes.name: Only the Worst: Trees Suck!
nodes.desc: For those who don't like flowers or trees :(.

nodes.name: Genetic Sampler
nodes.desc:
With this machine, you can extract a random trait from any bee, sapling, butterfly or flower. The bee/sapling/butterfly/flower will be destroyed in this process. Each process requires an empty gene sample and some labware.

The resulting sample is random, so make sure to recycle the extra gene samples you don't want.

nodes.name: Fastest Way to Get There
nodes.desc:
A GT++ Mutagenic frame will get your bees to their final destination faster than you can blink. Just remember to wear your rubber suit while making it!

[note]These will break in the alveary before they take effect since their durability is under 6. So you can only get to 125x, but I think that's enough, don't you?[/note]

nodes.name: Upgrade Your Forestry Backpack
nodes.desc:
With your woven silk you can upgrade your Forestry backpacks. Each Pack has 45 slots.

You need a carpenter, your old backpack and a bit of seed oil.

If the recipe isn't working, put the bag in a crafting grid to reset its NBT data. After removing anything in it of course.

nodes.name: A Rather Cruel Disposal
nodes.desc: You'll probably end up with a lot of excess drones while doing bees. (Or saplings if you do trees). Instead of throwing them away, you could also turn them into... something useful.

nodes.name: Woven Silk
nodes.desc:
Centrifuge your silky propoli to get some silk wisp at a chance of 60 percent. Put 9 silk wisp in the Forestry carpenter or GregTech assembler to get woven silk.

This fine fabric can be used for crafting Apiarist's Clothes or to upgrade a Forestry Backpacks to 45 slots.

nodes.name: A Backpack for Bees
nodes.desc: It's exactly what it says. It's also incredibly useful.

nodes.name: Frames
nodes.desc:
Untreated frames are the simplest frames. They do not work in bee houses, only in apiaries or alvearies. You will need them to craft bee houses.

They increase the bee's performance. Each untreated frame will double a bee's productivity.

nodes.name: Gene Database
nodes.desc:
Discovered genes are logged into the Gene Database. This handheld device lists all genes by the type of organism they apply to.

This device requires an EV circuit! Of all the things in the Binnie's Genetics line, it has the most technologically sophisticated requirement!

Use an Empty Serum Vial or Empty Serum Array on the different discovered traits to prepare a cocktail you want to inject into a Larvae. If you misclick, you can just click on the one you wanted without consequence.

nodes.name: IAADDS
nodes.desc:
Aka the Mega Apiary.

It has three primary modes (change with screwdriver) and two operation modes (change with shift+screwdriver):

INPUT MODE: Does not take power. Put your queens in the input bus to put them in the internal buffer.

OUTPUT MODE: Does not take power. Will give your bees back to the output bus.

OPERATING MODE - NORMAL: The processing time is 5 seconds. Uses 1 Amp LuV per queen. All bees are affected by 64x acceleration and 8 Production Upgrades as well as a Genetic Stabilizer Upgrade. The IAADDS also simulates a perfect environment for all bees.

You can provide royal jelly to increase the outputs. 1 royal jelly grants 5% bonus per bee. They will be consumed on each start of operation and be applied to that operation only. The maximum bonus is 200%. The normal bee stats still apply of course, though the IAADDS is able to provide a perfect environment for any bee.

OPERATING MODE - SWARMER: In this mode you can only insert 1 queen. The IAADDS will then slowly produce ignoble princesses for 100 royal jelly per operation. The base processing time is 1 minute but you can overclock this process. The base usage is 1 Amp IV.

[note]Yes you need thousands of queens, not princesses.[/note]

nodes.name: Living It Larvae
nodes.desc:
To play with Binnie's Genetics with bees, you'll need some Larvae, and a Hatchery block inside an Alveary is the only way to make them. There's a little side perk for having them: they produce at a much faster rate than you'd get from any one species' drones. Those leftovers can feed into the Gene Pool for extra raw DNA. Just remember to keep a few Larvae on standby for the actual genetic modification!

The bee you use in the Alveary should be whatever you intend to modify. It can be any kind if you intend to overwrite all the traits, but you probably should have it either be:

1. Some new species which will have everything else overwritten.
2. Some existing superbee that you want to switch to a new species.

The Larvae will eventually be hatched in an Incubator into a modified drone based on whatever genetic traits you have inserted into it.

nodes.name: Busy Bees Buzzing Boldly
nodes.desc:
These upgrades can significantly increase your production rate by keeping your bees from stopping production due to the environment.

Rain Shield - Can work through the rain
Lighting - Can work day and night
Alveary Heater - Increases temperature a flat 30% each (needs power)
Alveary Fan - Decreases temperature a flat 20% each (needs power)
Alveary Hygroregulator[sic] - Has two modes, water and lava
Lava - Temp+10%, Humidity-20%
Water - Temp-10%, Humidity+20%

Unfortunately, there's no way to make them like caves with a block.

nodes.name: Genepool
nodes.desc:
You will need to feed Raw DNA into a Polymerizer to prime your gene samples for injection into Larvae. The Genepool eats Enzyme and guzzles Ethanol in order to produce more Raw DNA than you could ever find even in a public gas station's restroom.

It is basically a chipper shredder for your leftover drones. You were hoarding them because you might need them some day, right? Today's that day! Whatever you put in here is going to go bye-bye. Make sure you keep some of your different drones around just in case.

It will also take saplings, flowers, and any excess Larvae you should be pumping out by now for modification and hatching.

nodes.name: Only the Best: Day and Night
nodes.desc: On your way to awesome bees, you have to collect only the best traits available. Bee working day and night, all night and all day long!

nodes.name: Impregnated Frames
nodes.desc:
Impregnated Frames are even better than untreated Frames.
Each frame doubles the bee's productivity. It has a longer durability than the untreated frame, but a shorter one compared to the proven frame.
